stem:
Priya lists four samples found in her home and school laboratory.

| sample | W | X | Y | Z |
| description | air in a balloon | pure distilled water | a brass (copper and zinc) plate | oxygen gas in a cylinder |

A mixture contains two or more substances physically mixed together, with each substance keeping its own properties. Which samples are mixtures?

teacher.key_rationale: Air (W) is a physical mixture of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases, each keeping its own properties. Brass (Y) is a physical mixture (alloy) of copper and zinc. Distilled water (X) is a single pure compound, and oxygen gas in the cylinder (Z) is a single pure element, so neither is a mixture. Hence W and Y only, option B. Option A traps students who treat any clear liquid as a mixture; option D traps students who assume any gas stored in a container must be a mixture.
